query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractSustained wear damages on the sliding surfaces of alloys are generally the culprit responsible for the failure of various mechanical systems. Inspired by high-entropy effects, here we deliberately deploy nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation in a Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 complex concentrated alloy, which yields ultralow wear rate within the order of 10−7 to 10−6 mm3/Nm between room temperature and 800 °C. Such remarkable wear resistance heretofore represents one of the highest wear resistance reported for the bulk alloys or composites, and originates from the multi-type adaptive friction interface protection governed by intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates. This cooperative heterostructure releases gradient frictional stress in stages upon wear at room temperature through the coexistence of multiple deformation pathways while activating a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer upon wear at 800 °C to minimize adhesive and oxidative wear. Our work uncovers a practical avenue for tailoring wear properties with multicomponent heterostructures over a wide temperature range.

cited_evidence.text: Figure 3A shows the Vickers hardness and wear rate variations of NiX and Ni3X as the temperature increases from RT to 800 °C. The hardness of NiX and Ni3X gradually decreases from 6.1 GPa and 4.3 GPa at RT to 3.7 GPa and 2.5 GPa at 800 °C, respectively. The high thermal hardness of NiX arises from the solid solution strengthening and the resultant heterostructures [,]. The trend in wear rate of the Ni3X with temperature is similar to that of the conventional alloys. Specifically, its wear rate increases from 1.1 × 10−5 mm3/Nm at RT to 4.2 × 10−5 mm3/Nm at 600 °C, but decreases afterward to 2.4 × 10−5 mm3/Nm at 800 °C. However, the wear rate of the NiX is basically maintained at the order of (10−7 to 10−6) mm3/Nm over the entire test temperature. In particular, it achieves ultra-low wear at RT (1.7 × 10−7 mm3/Nm) and 800 °C (9.1 × 10−7 mm3/Nm). decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys with improved wear resistance and low friction coefficients. Studies have shown that the addition of certain elements, such as W, can improve the wear resistance of these alloys. Additionally, the development of nanohierarchical architectures and composition undulation has been shown to yield ultralow wear rates. The use of surface engineering techniques, such as electroless copper plating, has also been explored to improve the interfacial bonding and properties of high-entropy alloy composites.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in developing high-entropy alloys with improved wear resistance, there is still a need to overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range, particularly in sliding evaluations from room temperature to 800 °C.
decision.why: The development of nanohierarchical architectures and composition undulation has been shown to yield ultralow wear rates, and this approach could be applied to the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix to improve its wear resistance and low friction coefficient throughout the full temperature range. This approach follows from the trend of research focused on developing high-entropy alloys with improved wear resistance and low friction coefficients, and it addresses the unsolved problem of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range.
